description:

HelloFresh, is seeking a Food Safety Quality Assurance Associate Manager. The FSQA Associate Manager  is responsible for all supporting food safety and quality assurance related internal audits in adherence with regulatory standards. The position supervises and supports the salaried FSQA Are Managers and hourly FSQA Associates. Additionally, the position supports developing, implementing, and managing food safety and quality control systems designed to ensure compliance with internal and regulatory requirements.

You Will…

• Ensure a high level of internal and external customer service. Supports investigating (and correct) internal issues and complaints relating to food safety and quality.

• Develop, motivate, engage, coach, and inspire a team of salaried FSQA supervisors and technicians, creating a positive team dynamic that encourages all employees to provide feedback and drive change from within. Provide all employees with the necessary tools, proper training, and corrective direction.

• Maintain accurate documentation regarding GMPs, HACCP, Holds, Calibration, standard operating procedures (SOP’s) and any other FSQA requirements.

• Coach and train FSQA employees, including Supervisors, to follow company procedures and processes, evaluate team productivity and accomplishments.

• Initiates RCA investigations, executes pending preventive and corrective action requests (CAPA), including nonconformities from holds, internal and external audits.

• Drive KPI improvements through a structured approach for continuous improvement.

You Are…

• Leadership: Train and develop a large group of salaried and hourly employees

• Performance Management: for assigned production lines.

• Problem Solving/Analysis, results driven

• Communication Proficiency: speak to employees with tact and diplomacy.

• Time Management: Tracking/monitoring production and maintaining productivity.

• Technical Capacity: Computer literacy to input information into the computer. Microsoft Office, Google sheets, Slack, and Warehouse management system (WMS) software.

You Have…

• Associate degree or related leadership work experience

• At least 3 years of work experience in quality assurance should be combined with a demonstrated track-record of accomplishments as an FSQA leader, and with satisfying customers in technology-driven, developing companies.

FSQ Values

• Act with honesty and integrity. Respect all coworkers and partners 

• Remain open. Share feedback, share mistakes and use them as learning opportunities with a focus on continuous improvement.

• Focus on relationships- Always handle yourself professionally and don’t burn bridges. No matter the situation, remain collaborative and always put your best foot forward.

• Ask questions, ask for help and share ideas. We are all in this together! 

• Escalate early and often 

Work Environment

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is in a manufacturing and assembly environment and is regularly exposed to cool and/or cold temperatures (0º - 40º Farhenheit). The employee is frequently exposed to fumes or airborne particles, moving mechanical parts and vibration. The noise level in the work environment and job sites can be loud. 

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, stoop, reach and lift for a minimum of 10 to 12 hours with or without reasonable accommodation. The employee is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects and/or tools. The employee is required to talk or hear with or without reasonable accommodation. 

The employee must regularly lift and move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and move up to 50 pounds with or without assistance. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and peripheral vision.

title: Senior Director of Tax
description:
Summary

Workiva is looking for a Sr. Director of Tax to shape and execute our global tax strategy. In this leadership role, you will lead our tax function while driving compliance, risk management, and strategic planning across all global operations. You will partner closely with executive leaders to support long-term business goals and ensure seamless financial execution. If you are a visionary tax leader ready to drive impact in a fast-paced technology environment, we want to hear from you.

What You'll Do

• Develop and execute the company's long-term global corporate income tax and indirect tax strategies, aligned with business growth, to manage the effective tax rate, cash taxes, and tax risk.

• Own the quarterly and annual global tax provision under ASC 740, including current and deferred taxes, valuation allowances, uncertain tax positions, and effective tax rate analysis. Be responsible for all tax-related SEC disclosures (10-K, 10-Q, proxy), including the income tax footnote, rate reconciliation, and MD&A discussion.

• Evaluate and apply new accounting and tax guidance, and document technical positions in memos.

• Partner with Controllership, Legal, Investor Relations, and external auditors on disclosures, audits, and SOX controls over income taxes.

• Oversee U.S. federal, state and local, and non-U.S. income tax compliance, and ensure timely, accurate filings globally.

• Own U.S. international tax positions and planning, including GILTI (NCTI), Subpart F, FDII (FDDEI), BEAT and foreign tax credits.

• Monitor Pillar Two and global minimum tax developments and readiness.

• Own transfer-pricing policy and manage tax exposure across intercompany arrangements; partner with Controller on intercompany accounting, documentation and elimination.

• Direct withholding, treaty and permanent establishment analysis on cross-border flows.

• Identify and execute tax planning opportunities, including credits, incentives, and entity structuring. Evaluate complex tax legislation changes to mitigate risks and capitalize on opportunities.

• Provide tax diligence, structuring, and integration support for M&A and financing transactions.

• Lead, coach, and develop a team of four tax professionals, reviewing their provision, compliance, and technical work for accuracy and quality.

• Advise executive leadership on tax risk and the tax implications of business initiatives.

What You'll Need

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

• Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license or Juris Doctor (JD) degree.

• 15+ years of progressive tax experience, including public accounting and in-house roles at a U.S. public multinational with at least five years of direct people management experience.

• Deep expertise in ASC 740 and SEC tax reporting, including drafting disclosures and working with external auditors.

• Proven ability to develop long-term tax strategy and to review and coach staff, ideally as a player-coach who stays close to technical work.

• Ability to multi-task, establish priorities, and work well with cross-functional teams under pressure.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex tax topics to non-tax executives.

• Proven track record in a dynamic environment, comfortable leading through change.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience leading tax teams within a public SaaS or high-growth technology company.

• Proven track record of managing complex international tax structures and M&A transactions.

•
Workiva platform experience.

• Master’s degree in Taxation (MST).

Travel Requirement & Working Conditions

• Up to 10% travel required for strategic team meetings and corporate events.

• Remote workspace setup.

How You’ll Be Rewarded
✅ Salary range in the US: $185,000.00 - $315,000.00 ✅ A discretionary bonus typically paid annually
✅ Restricted Stock Units granted at time of hire

We've established strategic partnerships with leading health plans including UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, and Aetna, plus a growing network of OBGYN clinics nationwide, positioning us for accelerated growth in the $50B+ women's behavioral health market.

embedding AI directly into our platform, using modern toolchains and processes that help engineers move faster while staying focused on high-impact problem solving.

work to reach it.

title: Nuuly - Sr DevOps Engineer
description:
Role Summary
Nuuly is searching for a DevOps Engineer to join our growing Platform Engineering team. We are looking for a candidate who will build and maintain features to enhance our systems, as well as serve as a deeply technical guide to our business team as they adopt features built by all engineering teams. Your goal will be to allow for seamless scalability of our production infrastructure and apply your technical expertise to help preclude growth concerns before they occur.
In this role, you will have the opportunity to build a breadth of experience with Kubernetes, Kafka, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). As a DevOps Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining our cloud infrastructure on GCP and managing containerized applications using Kubernetes. The ideal candidate should have more than 3 years of hands-on experience in DevOps practices, with a strong emphasis on GCP services and Kubernetes orchestration, and some experience in asynchronous message brokers (like Kafka & RabbitMQ). You will play a crucial role in optimizing our cloud environment and streamlining our development and deployment processes. This role will impact Nuuly's overall success and growth, driving our scalability, reliability, and efficiency.
Role Responsibilities
A typical week at Nuuly in this role may involve:

• Design, implement, and manage scalable and highly available cloud infrastructure on Google Cloud Platform, including Compute Engine, Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Storage, Cloud Networking, and Confluent Kafka.

• Collaborate with software development teams to establish efficient CI/CD pipelines, ensuring smooth and automated application deployments.

• Implement monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions to maintain the health, performance, and security of the cloud infrastructure.

• Collaborate with our engineering team to optimize our Kafka message broker to support our event-driven architecture and enhance system performance.

• Work with cross-functional teams to identify and address performance bottlenecks and optimize the overall system performance.

• Ensure the security of the cloud infrastructure and applications, implementing best practices and staying up-to-date with the latest security threats and mitigations.

A Phlebotomist serves patients by identifying the best method for retrieving blood; preparing specimens for laboratory testing; and performing screening procedures.  The Phlebotomist will also act as an operations manager for the designated patient service center (PSC) and oversee Natera’s phlebotomy program at the specified location.  Depending upon growth opportunities, this role may also require oversight of other phlebotomists as needed to support patient volume growth. *** IF YOUR STATE REQUIRES A PHLEBOTOMY LICENSE, IT MUST BE SENT IN WITH YOUR RESUME WITH YOUR APPLICATION ***

• Report any SPI or CAPA or NCR issues to internal Natera product management leadership team Assists with managing all phlebotomy equipment associated with the establishment and running of the patient service center[KC4] , may require heavy lifting of up to 50 pounds of supplies.

• May require reimbursable travel for stocking of supplies May include onboarding, training, and retraining of individual phlebotomists, as deemed necessary to support volume increases.

Evio is a highly unique pharmacy solutions company that was founded by and works closely with health plans to implement transformative (to cost, quality, access and experience) initiatives primarily focused on specialty and other high-cost medication solutions.

In 2020, a group of five amazing Blue Cross Blue Shield health plans that in total serve more than 20 million members recognized that the way medications get to patients needs significant reform-rapidly rising costs and massive system complexities are detrimental to patients and the entire industry. In 2025, Wellmark joined as Evio 's first non-founding investor and sixth owner health plan. Each company made, and continues to make, significant investments to establish Evio as an independent entity to lead this transformation.  

Evio has advanced analytics and contracting capabilities at scale , and a suite of digital tools , to power our high-cost medication solutions. Our solutions act as a self-reinforcing “flywheel” where each element strengthens and feeds into the next, and support an “Only Evio can do that,” mindset and prioritization.

Evio is also a company that has invested heavily in and been highly intentional about people, team and culture. We believe we have created a very special place to work and encourage candidates to observe and ask us about our culture and decide for themselves.

•
Empathy - The people our business serves always come first. We care for our teammates and put ourselves in the shoes of our health plan customers and the patients and clinicians our solutions benefit.

•
Diversity - We are committed to fostering a culture where everyone belongs and is valued for their background, experience and insights - one that encourages diversity of ideas, and is a nurturing, trusting, and accepting place for all.

•

In this role, you will collaborate with teammates across engineering, data, and client-facing teams to uncover insights from our data that help patients access high-cost medications in a simple and affordable way. You will use your analytical skills, innovative mindset, and tenacity to discover ways health plans can improve patients’ medication experiences. Your technical skills, curiosity, and health plan empathy will drive the evolution of Evio Insights to ensure it continues to meet the needs of health plan customers.
You will own the analytic lifecycle from problem to recommendation: you’ll translate ambiguous health plan problems into research questions, selecting the appropriate study or modeling approach, executing the analysis, and communicating clear, actionable recommendations.

• Explore data to identify signals, trends, utilization patterns, and anomali

title: Senior System Software Engineer - Security
description:
NVIDIA ’s invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. GPU deep learning ignited the modern AI era - with NVIDIA hardware and software acting as the foundation for the world’s most ambitious AI, robotics, and autonomous systems workloads. Today, we are the AI computing company. NVIDIA Data Center Systems - including DGX, HGX, and MGX platforms - deliver the world’s leading infrastructure for AI at scale. We are growing our teams with the most thoughtful, creative, and driven people on the planet.
NVIDIA is seeking a software engineer with systems software and security experience to join the Data Center Systems Software team. You will investigate and resolve product vulnerabilities and strengthen Secure Development Lifecycle (SDL) practices for platforms including HGX, DGX, and MGX.

What You’ll Be Doing:

• Investigate and reproduce vulnerabilities, assess exploitability and impact, and identify affected products and software versions.

• Assess third-party vulnerabilities and coordinate dependency updates, mitigations, or documented exceptions.

• Drive timely remediation with engineering owners and PSIRT Operations, including risk prioritization, escalation, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure.

• Develop or review security fixes, validate mitigations, develop regression tests, and coordinate updates across supported releases.

• Build automation for vulnerability triage, analysis, and tracking.

• Improve SDL practices through threat modeling, security design reviews, and other best-practices.

• Evangelize and drive SDL practices across NVIDIA data center software teams.
What We Need to See:

• BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

• 5+ years of relevant software or security engineering experience.

• Hands-on experience investigating and remediating vulnerabilities, including familiarity with CVSS scoring and CWE classification.

• Experience with secure development practices and security testing tools, such as static analysis, fuzzing, and software composition analysis.

• Familiarity with server firmware and systems software, plus experience building automation using Python or a comparable language.

• Experience with modern AI and Agents, including AI-forward mindset and proactive adoption of cutting-edge tools and techniques.

• The ability to drive resolution across distributed and diverse engineering teams.

• Solid technical foundation in embedded systems, with the ability to engage credibly in technical discussions around firmware architecture, memory safety, and hardware-software interfaces.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a strong preference for written communication that creates clarity and institutional memory for a remote team.

• Comfortable with ambiguity and complexity; you make sound decisions quickly with incomplete information and course-correct without friction.
Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:

• Product security experience with modern data center systems.

• Knowledge of secure boot, root of trust solutions, attestation, and related technologies such as UEFI, SPDM, or TCG DICE.

• A track record of improving SDL adoption or security automation across engineering teams.

• Demonstrated vulnerability research, security fixes, or open-source security contributions.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people on the planet working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you!
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 152,000 USD - 241,500 USD for Level 3, and 184,000 USD - 287,500 USD for Level 4. You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

What is Flagstone?

Flagstone is many things. An online savings platform, reinventing how individuals, businesses, and charities manage, protect, and grow their cash. A diverse group of people, bound by a collaborative spirit, and shared purpose. And lastly, a thriving, profitable business - where smart people do their best work.

Each definition shares a common thread: our unique culture. It’s our pride and joy. And our competitive advantage.

A feel for our culture:

To revolutionise the savings market, we need to be at our best. But high performance takes more than talent - it takes a culture of kindness, respect, and growth.

That’s why we’re building a diverse, inclusive community, where your voice is heard and valued. Where, with close support and room to develop, you can surpass even your own expectations. And be rewarded for it.

We may not change the world, but we can change the world of financial technology. And all it takes is a winning mix of drive, talent, and empathy. Our culture celebrates all three.

But enough about us. Let’s talk about you.

About the role

We’re looking for a Senior SecOps Engineer to take ownership of security operations at Flagstone. That covers everything from alert triage and incident response through to detection engineering and continuous improvement of how our SOC works.

This is a hands-on role that sits right at the operational end of security. You’ll spend real time in the alert queue, as well as building the detections and automation that make it better. You’ll be right in the middle of complex investigations and P1s, while also shaping how the function operates. You’ll also own our relationship with our managed SOC provider, setting the standards they work to rather than simply receiving their output.

About the team

You’ll sit within Security Engineering, reporting to our Security Team Leader. In this role you’ll own detection, triage and incident response, and act as the technical counterpart to our managed SOC provider. That means directing their scope, holding them to clear detection and response standards, and keeping ownership of anything escalated or high severity in house.

Does this sound like you?

You’re an engineer at heart. You’d rather write the detection than describe it, and you treat detections and automation like any other engineering work: version controlled, tested and documented. You’re the go to expert when something serious happens, and you can explain security risk just as clearly to engineers as to senior stakeholders.

You’re curious about new technology, AI included, and you have a clear view on where it genuinely helps and where it introduces risk.

What you’ll do

You’ll take ownership of our SOC operations and report on their performance and health to stakeholders across the business. You’ll run investigations and incident response for complex or high severity alerts, managing parallel workstreams, keeping stakeholders informed and running post incident reviews through to real changes in detections or process.

You’ll own the detection engineering backlog, building, tuning and retiring detections across Microsoft Sentinel and Defender, mapped to a coverage model such as MITRE ATT&CK. You’ll turn threat intelligence into detection logic and hunting activity, and drive our automation and SOAR maturity by building Logic App playbooks that reduce manual effort without losing judgement on the nuanced cases.

You’ll manage our managed SOC relationship day to day: defining scope and escalation criteria, reviewing performance against SLAs and acting as the technical escalation point for anything they can’t close. You’ll keep playbooks, escalation paths and documentation in shape so the practice scales beyond any one person, and you’ll track metrics like triage time, false positive rate and coverage gaps to drive continuous improvement.

You’ll also explore and introduce AI assisted tooling into SOC workflows, such as triage and enrichment copilots, detectio

title: Site Reliability Engineer (London)
description:
ABOUT EDRA

Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations.

We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Site Reliability Engineer to join our infrastructure team as the second-in-seat hire. Our team ships fast enough that we're starting to hit GitHub's rate limits, and infrastructure has to stay a month ahead of that. You'll be in key engineering meetings to ensure our infrastructure is ready before anyone asks, and to catch any decisions that may become infrastructure problems later.

This is not a ticket queue. You'll decide what gets built, push back when a managed service already does what someone wants to hand-roll, and invent when no pattern exists. You'll also write real software, not just the infrastructure code underneath it. We run containerized workloads on AWS and GCP, defined in infrastructure as code, with Postgres underneath. Some of our early infrastructure was built quickly before anyone owned it full-time. Part of the job is untangling that while keeping the team moving.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own our cloud infrastructure end to end: provisioning, security, reliability, and the infrastructure as code that defines it.

- Stay ahead of the engineering roadmap and have infrastructure ready before features land, working directly with the founders on where the infrastructure goes next

- Find where developers are waiting and remove the wait, whether that's CI, deployment, or environment spin-up. A person sat waiting is the most expensive thing we run, so rational spend on velocity is always on the table

- Run the reliability practice: monitoring, logging, and alerting that fails loudly with a clear signal, and the response when it does

- Lead large infrastructure builds and own our product security posture

- Make the build-vs-managed-service call, and hold the line when the simpler path is the right one

- Read and write Python well enough to see the infrastructure implications of what the team's building and catch problems before they land

- Own AI model safety and the governance of agentic processes. The team leans on agents for repetitive work, and you make sure nothing unsupervised can act on production infrastructure

- Hand capability to others, and support the team cross-functionally: build the tooling that lets engineers, GTM, the AI team, operations, and compliance do without you what today requires you

- Keep current across cloud and model providers so that when an engineer brings a new announcement, you have a credible answer

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

- 5 to 10 years in infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering

- Deep, recent experience running production workloads on AWS or GCP, defined in infrastructure as code. A wide toolkit with one or two areas you go deep on. You won't know every service, and we expect you to learn fast

- Python you've written in anger, in or alongside application code

- Postgres in production, and containerized workloads running under an orchestration platform

- A security instinct: you think about vulnerabilities continuously and patch constantly

- Evidence that you've held down an infrastructure function alone or in a very small team

- Work you can point to where you found an ambiguous problem, designed the fix, and made other people faster as a result

- Comfort saying no to senior people when the infrastructure demands it

RBONUS POINTS

- GCP experience, especially migrations or multi-cloud rollouts

- CloudWatch

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer - Tech Lead
description:
About OpenMined

OpenMined is a 501(c)(3) non-profit foundation that brings together leading minds in AI, security, and privacy technology to develop open-source solutions that transform how data can be accessed and shared. Founded in 2017, we've grown into a global community of over 18,000 members working to ensure that privacy protection and AI innovation reinforce each other rather than undermine one another. We are driven by a simple challenge: the most valuable data for solving humanity's greatest challenges remains locked away due to privacy concerns, and we can change that through technology rather than compromise.
About the Role
We're looking for a Senior / Staff Software Engineer to join OpenMined , a nonprofit building open-source infrastructure for federated AI.
You’ll lead our 😱 ScreamingFace squad, the team that makes this vision real by building the internet's first leaderboard for fusion models (ensembles) and the open toolkit supporting benchmark evaluations for fusion models. Today, claims that the newest solo LLM beats the others are everywhere, and almost none of them can be checked or compared with the performance achieved by combining LLMs into more powerful fusion models. Results are self-reported, expensive to rerun, and hard to pick apart. We think there’s a better standard: every fusion and benchmark run compiles to a single line of text that anyone can replay for almost nothing, and a score counts only once someone else can reproduce it. The ScreamingFace toolkit is the open-source Python library and engine, leveraging our URL4 protocol, to let any researcher (a frontier lab, a university group, an independent builder) compose ensembles and routers across open and closed models, using their own keys, and grade them against pinned benchmarks. The ScreamingFace leaderboard is the public map of the quality-cost frontier, backed by a shared cache that makes every result on it cheap to verify and easy to build on.
This is a hands-on technical leadership role . You understand the long term vision. You write code. You make architecture decisions. You set engineering standards by example. You're the most experienced engineer on the squad, the person others look to for production-quality judgment, and the voice that connects this team's decisions with the organization's broader platform strategy.
The squad is talented and mission-driven and looking to strengthen its ability to continuously ship production software. You bring this production muscle: the instinct for what scales, the judgment about what to build and what to kill, and the craft to raise the team's standard through code review, pairing, and architectural guidance rather than mandates.
If you're motivated by building distributed systems that matter, mentoring brilliant people who are just getting started, and making hard technical calls in a fast-moving nonprofit that's trying to change how the world shares data - we'd love to hear from you.
You'll work most closely with Kevin McDonough, Head of Engineering.
This is an independent contractor engagement, roughly a full-time commitment, with an initial 12-month term we expect to renew. You set your own schedule, but we need your working hours to overlap substantially with US Eastern business hours (your local time within about one hour of ET).

• Drive production readiness through deployment monitoring, error handling, graceful degradation, and operational runbooks.

• Be a force multiplier by establishing, demonstrating, and mentoring the team to establish norms around engineering best practices (including system design for modularity, security, reliability, & scalability), code quality, and delivery to production.

title: Sustainable Forest Management Consultant – Thailand

Location: Thailand

PUR Description
PUR is a global, impact-focused B-Corp specializing in the development of environmental restoration projects, known as ‘nature-based solutions’ (NbS). Since 2008, we have been helping the world’s largest organizations meet their ESG targets, reduce their environmental footprint, and regenerate the ecosystems they depend on across complex supply chains. Having developed over 45 projects in more than 30 countries, PUR is recognized as both a pioneer and leader in a sector that is now at the forefront of global efforts to address the ongoing climate and biodiversity crisis.
At the heart of our mission is a commitment to fostering and operationalizing insetting strategies-interventions by companies within their own value chains designed to reduce GHG emissions while creating positive impacts for communities, landscapes, and ecosystems. By championing this insetting approach, we aim to create a holistic range of benefits that extend beyond ecological restoration, encompassing social and economic dimensions through enhanced agricultural yields and resilience to climate change-induced stresses, among others.
One of the distinctive features of our work is our ability to tailor projects to the specific needs of different regions and communities. By recognizing the unique characteristics of each ecosystem and the cultural context of the communities involved, we ensure our initiatives are contextually relevant and have a meaningful and sustainable impact. All our projects are developed in close collaboration with local actors, including cooperatives, NGOs, governments, and corporations. Today, we employ 200 staff across 16 countries with key offices in Paris (HQ) and Toronto.
Thamma Raksa Project | PUR

PUR is looking for an experienced Sustainable Forest Management Consultant to support the development of a comprehensive Sustainable Forest Management Plan (SFMP) for the Thamma Raksa Project in Isaan, Thailand .
The project focuses on agroforestry and small-scale forest plantations across several provinces in Northeast Thailand. The consultant will develop practical forest management, selective harvesting, post-harvesting and farmer training approaches that support long-term forest health, carbon storage and farmer needs.
About the Assignment
The main objective of this consultancy is to develop a practical and comprehensive Sustainable Forest Management Plan aligned with:

• Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) Version 5.0

• VM0047

• ABACUS Label

• Symbiosis Quality Criteria

The plan will cover different planting models, tree species and ecological and socio-economic contexts across Isaan, Thailand.
Key Responsibilities
The consultant will be responsible for:

• Developing the Sustainable Forest Management Plan for the Thamma Raksa project.

• Developing appropriate maintenance practices , including pruning, thinning, weeding and pest management.

• Developing guidelines for selective harvesting , including tree selection, harvesting volumes, timing and methods.

• Conducting tree growth, biomass and harvesting analysis to support harvesting schedules and carbon-stock projections.

• Developing recommendations for post-harvesting management, replanting and natural regeneration .

• Considering Thailand's forestry regulations, land tenure and socio-economic context.

• Developing a practical monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) framework .

• Supporting farmer engagement and developing practical training materials.

• Translating technical recommendations into practical guidance for farmers and field implementation partners.

Key Deliverables
The consultancy will include:

• Sustainable Forest Management Plan - English, Word and PDF

• Farmer-friendly summaries - English and Thai

• Harvesting Schedule & Biomass Growth Impact Dataset - Exc

title: Staff Pricing Analyst, B2B
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

Relay delivers 400,000 parcels a day through people who don't work for us: van drivers who choose their own shifts, local shops that hold parcels, and couriers who take them to the door. We went from 3,000 parcels a day in London to 400,000 across the UK in under three years.

Most delivery companies sell on price and volume, and find out later whether a client made them money. Sales teams are measured on what they sign, not on what a signing is worth. Relay wants every client, and every new shop in the network, to be one we'd choose again.

That is harder for us than for most, because what a client is worth depends on how their parcels flow through a network that's still growing. Engineering and analytics engineering build what you design.

SALES HIGHLIGHTS

- You own decision-making, not the model: you decide what a client or shop is worth and which signings sales should chase. The sales lead acts on your calls.

- What is a new client or a new shop worth, when its value depends on where it sits in a network that changes every month? What would you build so sales knows before it signs?

- Which signings become partners who do well with us, and what does that tell sales to look for?

- The quarter's target is set. What has to close by when for it to hold, and what would tell you early that it won't?

- A whole area, not a slice: you decide how sales values what it wins, and the result shows in what we sign next.

- Analytics at the front, not in support: the squad's roadmap follows the analysis, in a data team of about 30 across analytics, operational research and data science.

THE OPPORTUNITY

As a Staff Pricing Analyst, B2B at Relay, you'll:

- Decide which Sales problems are real and which only look real, before anyone builds a fix.

- Design how Sales decides: which signals count, what a client or shop is worth, and what good looks like.

- Tell the sales lead what to change and what to stop, and get a decision.

- Build the thing that decides: data applications, monitors and alerts, not decks, using Claude and agents to ship your own tools.

- Go and look when the numbers and the street disagree: a new shop, a client's parcels at the sort centre.

- Get the missing data built, and prove whether each change worked. In a year, sales chooses what to go after on measures you built, and can see whether the quarter will land before it ends.

WE'RE LOOKING FOR CANDIDATES WHO…

- Have owned B2B pricing or commercial decisions and their number, rather than maintaining sales dashboards.

- Have built, hands on, the first version of how a company values a customer or a deal: unit economics, lifetime value, or what it costs to win one.

- Have seen their work acted on: a leader changed a plan, a team adopted your method, or sales went after different deals because of it.

- Have got records created by teams who didn't report to you, and know how long it takes.

title: Clinical Data Engineer (Application Engineer)
description:
Department Overview
The mission of the Information Technology Group (ITG) is to provide and support technology and information services that enable OHSU to be a national leader in health and science innovation. The work of the Business Intelligence & Advanced Analytics Division (BIAA) is to deliver meaningful analytic solutions by bringing together data, systems, and people to enhance the work and lives of OHSU members and the communities we serve.
Function/Duties of Position
The Clinical Data Engineer sits on the clinical data team within the broader Clinical Business Intelligence unit, alongside analysts, engineers, administrators, and architects. This position builds new clinical data warehousing solutions, data transformations, and data integration assets, and supports the changes, enhancements, and maintenance of existing assets in support of OHSU clinical data initiatives.
You will work closely with cross-functional teams - clinical and operational stakeholders, data architects, and IT specialists - to develop robust data pipelines, implement data quality controls, and deliver trustworthy data that supports clinical decision-making. Development happens primarily in the Epic Caboodle Console, Microsoft SQL Server tools, and Microsoft Fabric Data Engineering tools, with Azure DevOps for version control, code management, and deployment. Duties may extend to other cloud data engineering tools, such as Apache Airflow, as needed.
Key responsibilities include:

• Design and develop ETL pipelines that extract, transform, and load clinical data from a variety of sources into structures suitable for analysis.

• Implement data quality controls that validate, monitor, and maintain the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of clinical data across the pipeline lifecycle.

• Contribute to the growth of the OHSU Caboodle Data Warehouse by designing, developing, testing, and implementing custom clinical data models.

• Partner with BI architects, developers, analysts, and customers (practice managers, data scientists, quality analysts) to build and publish data models, ETL processes, Lakehouses, Warehouses, Notebooks, and metadata using the Epic Caboodle Console and third-party ETL tools.

• Develop data feeds using SSIS or similar tools, ensuring appropriate security review and transport consistent with information privacy and security requirements, business associate agreements, and data use agreements.

• Document warehouse content in the Caboodle Console and the Analytics Marketplace so users can determine what data exists, how it is defined, and how it traces back to Epic Clarity.

• Troubleshoot ETL failures, data anomalies, and warehouse issues surfaced by automated monitoring, other developers, and end users; resolve or escalate through established processes and communicate status to affected groups.

• Recommend improvements to ETL processes, tool sets, data models, and monitoring techniques that increase reliability and efficiency.

• Deploy warehouse content using approved Azure DevOps systems and processes, and follow approved SDLC practices throughout.

• Manage assigned projects by building timelines, identifying risks and milestones, and reporting status.

• Respond to and track issues in Jira Service Desk, gathering information from customers and triaging to resolution.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, a related field, or a clinical field and six years of work-related experience in the information technology field or a combination of clinical or operational healthcare environments; OR

• Associate’s degree in computer science, a related field, or a clinical field and seven years of work-related experience in the information technology field or a combination of clinical or operational healthcare environments; OR

• Eight years work related experience in the information technology field or a combination of clinical or operational healthcare environments; OR

title: Release Train Engineer / Developer - Remote EU/EEA
description:
This is a remote position.
Release Train Engineer / Developer
About the role
We are hiring a Release Train Engineer / Developer with strong mainframe skills to coordinate and deliver releases across a major lending platform built on FIS ALS. This is a delivery-and-coordination role at the centre of the programme: you will orchestrate the release train across development, testing, infrastructure and business teams, and act as the communication bridge between Product Management, Product Owners, Scrum Teams, business users and leadership.

Work authorization This role is open to candidates with EU/EEA citizenship or existing, unrestricted right to work in the EU - no visa sponsorship is provided. We are particularly keen to hear from candidates holding a Romanian, Polish, Bulgarian, Czech, Portuguese or Spanish passport (or other EU member state passport). This is a fully remote role.

Responsibilities

Release coordination

• Coordinate release schedules across ALS development, testing, infrastructure and business teams.

• Plan and orchestrate SIT, UAT, Pre-Production and Production deployment activities.

• Manage ALS upgrades, patches and vendor (FIS) releases.

• Ensure regulatory and compliance-related changes are delivered on schedule.

ALS-specific delivery

• Coordinate change across ALS modules: Loan Origination, Credit Administration, Commercial Lending, Loan Servicing, and interfaces with Core Banking and Treasury systems.

• Collaborate with FIS/vendor support teams, business SMEs, testing teams and infrastructure teams.

• Manage code promotion, environment readiness and cut-over planning.

Communication & governance

• Act as the bridge between Product Management, Product Owners, Scrum Teams, business users and leadership.

• Track dependencies, risks and readiness across the release train; represent changes at change-approval forums (CAB).

Requirements

Essential skills

• Strong mainframe skills - COBOL, JCL, CICS, DB2 (and ideally Coolgen / IEF, the technology underpinning ALS).

• Experience coordinating releases across dev, test, infrastructure and business teams.

• Hands-on planning of SIT / UAT / Pre-Prod / Production deployments and cut-over.

• Exposure to FIS ALS or a comparable lending / core-banking platform.

• Change and configuration management (e.g. Endevor / Changeman), scheduling (Control-M / CA7), Connect:Direct.

• Comfortable managing tiered environments (Dev / Test / UAT / Pre-Prod / Production / DR).

Desirable

• Release Train Engineer experience in a SAFe / Agile environment (PI planning, scrum-of-scrums).

• Lending domain knowledge (loan origination, servicing, commercial lending, credit).

• Experience with vendor release cycles and patch management on a packaged banking product.

• Core Banking and Treasury interface integration experience.

Benefits

What we offer

• Long-term engagement on a high-visibility lending transformation.

• Fully remote - nearshore working.

• Competitive day rate (aligned to channel and discussed on application).

title: Senior Software Engineer (m/w/d) für Individualsoftware
description:
über uns
Was für einen Kunden eine Ausnahme ist, gehört für den nächsten zum Tagesgeschäft. Wir entwickeln Individualsoftware für mittelständische Unternehmen aus Industrie, Handel und Versicherungen. Gemeinsam betreuen wir mehrere Kundenprojekte - so lernst du unterschiedliche Geschäftsabläufe kennen und gestaltest Anwendungen für Web, Mobilgeräte und Desktop.
Als Senior Software Engineer klärst du mit den Fachleuten auf Kundenseite, was die Software im Alltag leisten muss. Du gestaltest die Architektur mit und setzt deine Entscheidungen selbst im Code um.
das gibt es zu tun

•
Fachliche Anforderungen verstehen. Du klärst mit den Fachleuten auf Kundenseite, welche Abläufe die Anwendung unterstützen soll. Du übersetzt Geschäftsregeln und Sonderfälle in ein tragfähiges Softwaredesign.

•
Architektur gestalten und selbst entwickeln. Du entscheidest mit, wie eine Anwendung aufgebaut ist, wie ihre Komponenten zusammenspielen und wo sie an bestehende Systeme angebunden wird. Deine Entscheidungen bringst du selbst in den Code.

•
Anwendungen durchgängig entwickeln. Je nach Projekt entwickelst du Geschäftslogik und Schnittstellen mit C# und .NET oder mit TypeScript und Node.js. Dabei arbeitest du an Webanwendungen ebenso wie an nativen Apps für Mobilgeräte oder Desktop.

•
Mit Daten arbeiten. Du entwirfst relationale Datenmodelle, die fachliche Zusammenhänge verständlich abbilden. Wenn eine Abfrage mit wachsender Datenmenge langsam wird, gehst du der Ursache auf den Grund.

•
Bestehende Software weiterentwickeln. Du findest Wege, neue Anforderungen sauber in eine gewachsene Codebasis zu integrieren. In Code-Reviews teilst du deine Erfahrung und machst technische Entscheidungen im Team nachvollziehbar.

das bringst du mit

• Du hast mindestens fünf Jahre Erfahrung in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung. Besonders wertvoll ist für uns, wenn du bereits Individualsoftware für Kunden entwickelt oder an komplexen Fachanwendungen gearbeitet hast.

• Du bringst ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Informatik, Informationstechnik oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation mit.

• Dein technischer Schwerpunkt liegt in C# und .NET oder in TypeScript und Node.js. In einem der beiden Stacks hast du fundierte Praxiserfahrung, mit dem anderen hast du bereits gearbeitet.

• Kenntnisse in Vue.js, React oder Angular sind ebenso willkommen wie Erfahrung mit nativen Mobil- oder Desktop-Anwendungen. Java-Kenntnisse sind ein weiteres Plus.

• Du hast Erfahrung mit Softwarearchitektur, wendest Clean-Code-Prinzipien an und kannst begründen, wann ein Entwurfsmuster ein konkretes Problem einfacher löst.

• Du kennst dich gut mit relationalen Datenbanken aus und hast praktische Erfahrung mit mindestens einem dieser Systeme gesammelt - PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle oder IBM DB2.

• Du bist offen für moderne Entwicklungswerkzeuge und Agentic Coding. Du hast Lust, Coding-Agenten gezielt einzusetzen, und prüfst ihre Vorschläge mit demselben Anspruch wie deinen eigenen Code.

• Du kannst technische Entscheidungen im Team und gegenüber Kunden verständlich erklären.

• Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und Englisch

das bekommst du

•
Start & Welcoming so wie du es verdienst! Ein strukturiertes Onboarding mit echten Ansprechpersonen - damit du vom ersten Tag an durchstartest.

•
Remote Work Homeoffice innerhalb von Deutschland oder Arbeiten in unserem modernen Büro in Offenburg? Arbeite so, wie es für dich am besten passt.

•
A I-first arbeite n, statt darüber zu reden  Lizenzen für Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot & Co. stellen wir. Neue Tools und Modelle darfst du ausprobieren, statt sie zu beantragen - und deine Erkenntnisse verändern, wie das ganze Team arbeitet. 

•
Betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit 20 % Arbeitgeberzuschuss - deutlich über dem gesetzlichen Standard.

title: M&A Legal Intern - Spring 2027
description:
Established in 2015, Create Music Group is a leading music and entertainment company. The company operates as a record label, distribution company, and entertainment network which generates over 15 billion music streams each month on DSP’s. Named #2 on the Inc 5000 Fastest Growth Companies in America in 2020, the company has grown exponentially by leveraging its owned IP with its media and technology platform. The company works with superstar artists, major and independent record labels, and global media brands. It operates a number of companies including Label Engine, one of the largest independent music distribution platforms in the world, with over 75,000 artists and 5,000 label clients; and Flighthouse, a digital entertainment brand focused on Gen Z, which has more than 300 million followers across social media. Create Music Group is based in Hollywood, CA and has 400 employees worldwide.

Job Summary

Create Music Group is seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Legal Intern to join its M&A Legal Group. This unique internship offers a chance to gain hands-on experience in music-related transactions and corporate legal work. The intern will work directly under the guidance of the VP and the Director of M&A Legal Affairs, contributing to a range of strategic initiatives. The role primarily focuses on acquisitions, intellectual property, and corporate compliance, with a particular emphasis on music catalog acquisitions.

This is a part-time, fully remote internship specifically designed for current graduate students for Spring 2027. Candidates must be eligible to work in the U.S. and be available for 15-20 hours per week over a 3-month period.

Responsibilities

• Assisting in the drafting and review of asset purchase agreements, letters of direction, and other related transactional documents.

• Conducting legal research and due diligence on potential acquisition targets.

• Supporting the preparation and submission of copyright registrations with the U.S. Copyright Office.

• Aiding in the management and maintenance of corporate organizational documents and ensuring ongoing compliance (e.g., filings, entity records, debt compliance).

• Reviewing and revising non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with prospective partners and counterparties.

• Organizing and tracking deal documents and legal correspondence.

• Collaborating cross-functionally with finance, operations, and A&R teams on various transaction-related tasks.

• Providing administrative support for ongoing legal projects as assigned by the VP and the Director of M&A Legal Affairs.

• Opportunities to support additional tasks based on the intern’s interest and availability.

Qualifications

• Possess a strong interest in M&A, intellectual property, and the music/media industry.

• Demonstrate excellent legal writing, organizational, and communication skills.

• Ability to handle confidential information with the utmost discretion.

• Exhibit a detail-oriented, proactive, and collaborative mindset.

• Prior experience in transactional, corporate, or entertainment law, including previous internships, is considered a plus.

Pay Scale

• The pay scale for this position is designated as the local hourly minimum wage depending on the candidate’s work location.

Program Details

• Start Date: Spring 2027 Term

• Length: 3-4 months

• Schedule: 10-23 hours per week

title: Software Engineer, Frontier Data Products
description:
ABOUT MERCOR

Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. We build the infrastructure that enables frontier AI labs and enterprises to train, evaluate, and improve AI on real-world professional work. More than five million experts have joined our network, and we pay out over $5 million daily for their knowledge and expertise.

We built our training and evaluation infrastructure alongside the world’s leading AI labs. Now, we’re bringing those capabilities to enterprises across industries, enabling them to train, evaluate, and improve AI using their own expertise and standards. Our APEX benchmarks measure how AI performs on economically valuable work, while our enterprise evaluations and post-training capabilities turn those insights into measurable improvements across real-world workflows.

Our work sits at the intersection of frontier AI, human expertise, and real-world application. We’re solving problems few companies have encountered, with the opportunity to influence what the world’s most advanced AI systems become capable of doing. We’re looking for people who bring different perspectives, take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and hold themselves to an exceptionally high standard. You’ll have the opportunity to do consequential work alongside talented colleagues who challenge one another, collaborate openly, and share a commitment to excellence.

Mercor is profitable and recently raised a $750 million Series D at a $20 billion valuation. We work in person five days a week in San Francisco, New York, and London.

ABOUT MERCOR

Mercor is defining the future of work. We partner with leading AI labs and enterprises to provide the human intelligence essential to AI development.

Our vast talent network trains frontier AI models in the same way teachers teach students: by sharing knowledge, experience, and context that can't be captured in code alone. Today, more than 30,000 experts in our network collectively earn over $2 million a day.

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society.

Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our new San Francisco headquarters.

About the Role
Frontier AI companies are increasingly bottlenecked on expert judgment and high-quality data workflows. This team builds the production systems that capture, coordinate, and validate that work at scale - directly between a customer request and the output that ships.
These are long-running, stateful systems. A single job can stay live for days, interleaving automated steps, model inference, and expert review. A step marked "done" can be reopened, re-reviewed, and redone - so "completed" is not always final, state has to tolerate late mutation, and correctness has to survive humans and models disagreeing with each other.
This is a backend systems and orchestration problem: distributed state machines, not pipelines. The architecture is not set. Early engineers will decide what it becomes, and the loop between "I shipped this" and "this mattered" is short.
What You'll Do

- Design services and state models for multi-stage workflows that fan out across automated processing and expert reviewers, then reconcile results into a coherent whole

- Build orchestration primitives - retries, failure recovery, idempotency, auditable state transitions - for jobs that run far longer than a request and can be partially redone after the fact

- Integrate model inference into production workflows without sacrificing debuggability or human oversight

- Build the APIs and tooling that let product, operations, and ML teams operate, debug, and trust these systems at scale

- Own reliability and observability for workflows where a silent failure means a c

title: Junior Registered Dietitian Manager
description:
Location: Remote - United States
Employment type: Full-time
Base salary range: $80,000 - $88,000 per year, plus performance-based incentives
The opportunity
Sensibly Sprouted is hiring a Junior Registered Dietitian Manager to build and lead a team of dietitians providing outpatient Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT). You’ll play a central role in interviewing and selecting team members, coach their development, and shape how your team delivers care.
This is a developmental management role for dietitians ready to move into formal people leadership. Prior management experience is not required.
Internally, this position is called Junior Lead. You’ll report to the Chief Dietetics Officer and have management authority from day one. The broader leadership team will support you as you handle increasingly complex team, financial, and operational decisions. Your focus is team leadership; you may provide patient care when needed, but the role has no fixed caseload.
What you’ll do

• Take a lead role in interviewing, selecting, and onboarding dietitians as you build your team.

• Coach and develop team members, set expectations, give feedback, and address performance concerns.

• Progressively assume ownership of the team’s profit and loss (P&L), including revenue, expenses, and profitability, while managing retention and productive capacity with leadership support. Use financial and performance data to guide decisions.

• Reinforce clinical, documentation, scheduling, and operational standards, partnering with Clinical Excellence on training needs.

• Manage team workflows and priorities, involving senior leadership when decisions require their input.

What you’ll bring

• A Registered Dietitian (RD) or Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) credential.

• Applicable state licensure, or eligibility to obtain required licensure.

• Demonstrated ability to coach others, lead initiatives, and improve team performance. A prior manager title is not required.

• Sound judgment, clear communication, dependable follow-through, and comfort using performance data to guide decisions.

• Authorization to work in the United States without employer sponsorship.

Your growth
Junior Lead provides support and feedback as you develop the judgment and independence required for Lead. After at least four quarters, you may be evaluated for advancement based on demonstrated Lead-level capability, sustained performance, and organizational need. Advancement is not automatic. Upon promotion, your base pay moves into the Lead salary range.
Benefits
Eligible team members receive medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer healthcare contributions; a 401(k) with a 3% employer non-matching contribution; paid time off and holidays; and professional development support. Sensibly Sprouted also pays required professional liability insurance, state licensure fees, and CDR registration and renewal fees where applicable.
About Sensibly Sprouted

We are a team of registered dietitians providing personalized, evidence-based nutrition counseling and Medical Nutrition Therapy. Our care emphasizes ongoing patient relationships and practical changes that fit real life.
Sensibly Sprouted is an equal opportunity employer and provides reasonable accommodations to qualified applicants.
Salary: $80,000 - $88,000 per year Originally posted on Himalayas
